MEMORANDUM

TO: Office of the University Registrar; Council of Academic Deans
FROM: Office of Institutional Data & Governance
DATE: October 26, 2023
SUBJECT: Comprehensive Roster of Affiliated Academic Programs for Organizational Administration

1.0 Executive Summary

This document provides a definitive internal roster of academic programs associated with our university organization. Each strategic unit is cataloged with its official designation and corresponding registry identifier for administrative and communication clarity. The following profiles are to be considered the single source of truth for all inter-departmental correspondence and student information system management.

2.0 Academic Program Profiles

The academic program for Soils and Sustainable Land Systems (Registry ID: recgbn2VvmEBWmuUi) is a critical interdisciplinary unit. This program is instrumental in supporting the university's agricultural extension services and environmental policy research. The department's annual fall harvest festival is a popular campus event, though its planning is managed entirely by a student-led committee.

Regarding the vocational track for IT Support and Web Development, registered under identifier rec7SRmmw3oovHndK, this program maintains one of the highest post-graduation employment rates. Its curriculum is continuously updated to reflect current industry demands for cloud computing and cybersecurity specialists. We have received confirmation that the carpeting in the main computer lab is scheduled for deep cleaning over the winter break.

The program initially logged in the system as 'Financial Markets' has been corrected and finalized. The official designation is now Finance (Registry ID: rec0xRZtkzxrg8kj2), a change made to better encompass its broader focus on corporate and personal finance theory. This unit works closely with the university's endowment fund, providing students with unique hands-on portfolio management experience. The lead professor for the capstone course is also a nationally ranked chess player, a hobby he pursues in his personal time.

An administrative review of vocational certifications revealed a minor discrepancy in program naming. What was previously cataloged as 'Welding Arts' has been formally amended to Welding Technology (recr0WVEPZ08hl4Wt). This program is vital for regional workforce development, supplying skilled technicians to the manufacturing and construction sectors. Furthermore, the program's workshop recently had its primary ventilation system upgraded, a project completed two weeks ahead of schedule.

The unit for Animal, Dairy, and Veterinary Sciences (Registry ID: recIn8odwOmxEgrBl) serves as a cornerstone of the College of Agriculture. It consistently attracts high levels of federal research funding for its work in animal health and food production. The department’s break room coffee machine was recently replaced with a newer model that also dispenses hot water for tea.

We have a listing for the discipline of Philosophy (Registry ID: recGvuGMS6k5vjnst), which forms a core component of the humanities curriculum. The program fosters critical thinking and analytical skills applicable across a wide range of professions. Enrollment figures for its introductory courses have remained remarkably stable over the past five fiscal years.

The academic unit for Applied Economics (Registry ID: recFQ1RMc4EjTQFOi) is distinguished by its focus on econometric modeling and practical policy analysis. This program provides essential data-driven insights for both public and private sector partners. The department's administrative assistant has a noted collection of decorative succulents on their office windowsill.

A clerical error in the course catalog from the previous academic year listed the language program as 'Spanish Literature'. This has been rectified in the current master roster to the broader, more accurate title of Spanish (rec8TIqmun4d5vsvN). The program's immersion and study abroad components are consistently rated as highlights of the student experience. The department is also known for its vibrant participation in the campus-wide holiday decorating contest each December.

The program for Business (Registry ID: recxK3MHQFbR9J5uO) functions as a generalized pathway for students prior to their declaration of a more specific concentration. It provides a foundational understanding of market principles, management, and corporate ethics. Interestingly, the vending machines in the business school building were recently switched to a new vendor, resulting in a different selection of snack foods.

An update was required for the engineering school's roster; the program previously entered as 'Electrical Systems' is now correctly recorded as Electrical Engineering (rec7BxKpjJ7bNph3O). This strategic unit is heavily involved in robotics and renewable energy systems research, securing significant patents for the university. The department head is an avid birdwatcher and maintains a detailed log of campus avian life.

The program for Biochemistry (Registry ID: reckPDbeLc8ogfvWo) is a joint-effort discipline that bridges the biological and chemical sciences. Its research is fundamental to advancements in medicine and biotechnology. The primary lecture hall for this major, Henderson Hall Room 201, recently had its projector bulb replaced.

Initial registration data for the business college marked a program as 'Bookkeeping'. Following a curriculum audit, this has been updated to its formal, accredited title: Accounting (recuv3Nj4esENfIZW). This unit is essential for maintaining our AACSB accreditation and is known for its rigorous CPA examination preparation. The department's annual potluck is renowned for its diverse array of international dishes.

The unit for Music Therapy (Registry ID: recXNkQGvzEThZhG3) is a specialized health professions program that combines clinical practice with artistic skill. It has established partnerships with local hospitals and care facilities, providing students with invaluable practical experience. The department’s piano tuner is scheduled for their semi-annual visit next month.

A review of program names in the College of Agriculture and Applied Sciences noted a minor inconsistency. The program once labeled 'Food Systems' has been officially corrected to Food Science (rec6bKTSnOJAPwoXV). This discipline focuses on the chemistry, microbiology, and engineering of food production and safety. The department’s main laboratory recently passed its annual safety inspection with no citations.

The program for Dietetics (Registry ID: recd4JTuI0ssyoz07) is a professional track focused on nutrition and its impact on human health. Graduates are prepared for careers as registered dietitians in clinical and community settings. The department’s student association is organizing a campus-wide healthy bake sale next month to raise funds for charity.

We have the interdisciplinary program International Studies (Registry ID: recRA9IxLl6eKPsJX) on the roster. This unit combines political science, economics, and cultural studies to analyze global affairs. Its Model United Nations team has consistently performed well in national competitions for the last several years.

The program for Forest Ecology and Management (Registry ID: rec1N0upiVLy5esTO) is critical for training professionals in natural resource conservation and stewardship. This program leverages the university's extensive land holdings for field research and hands-on learning. The department's fleet of off-road vehicles recently underwent routine maintenance.

A minor correction was processed for the pre-law track; it was previously listed as 'Constitutional Law'. The official, broader designation is Law and Constitutional Studies (recxRBSgVYeSEGvyo). This program provides a strong foundation for students intending to pursue graduate studies in law or public policy. The department’s lounge is noted for having particularly comfortable armchairs, a frequent topic of student conversation.

The program for Landscape Architecture (Registry ID: recsiWnUNDT2kmOnr) blends artistic design with environmental science. Students in this major are responsible for several campus beautification projects, including the redesign of the main quad's botanical garden. The drafting studio for this program recently acquired three new large-format printers.

An audit of the health sciences college's offerings confirmed a naming convention update. The program formerly known as 'Community Health' is now officially designated as Public Health (recE5U2qZOYMmmnKZ). Its focus is on disease prevention and health education at the population level, a critical area of study. The building housing this department is slated for window washing on the first Monday of next month.

The unit for Global Communication (Registry ID: recFmin5MqRH5YC7m) examines how information and culture are exchanged across international borders. The curriculum includes media studies, rhetoric, and intercultural relations. The department’s newsletter, "The Global Gazette," is published bi-weekly and has a small but dedicated readership.

We have the specialized education program Physics Teaching (Registry ID: recVYIFAwjT91pnv7) on record. This unit prepares students for state licensure to teach physics at the secondary school level. It combines rigorous subject matter expertise with pedagogical training.

The program for Management Information Systems (Registry ID: recdem96jNnpiXfsH) is located at the intersection of business and technology. This unit trains students to design and manage the data systems that support modern organizations. The department’s student chapter of the Association for Information Systems is one of the most active on campus.

A systems reconciliation confirmed the official name for a key technology program. An earlier entry labeled 'Computer Programming' has been updated to the more comprehensive title, Computer Science (recrVJyCL0EoMvn6V). This program is central to the university's STEM initiatives and has seen a significant increase in enrollment over the past three years. The department is currently beta-testing a new automated system for booking student advising appointments.

The program for Criminal Justice (Registry ID: recaCi0HRhiGc6Pi7) provides a comprehensive study of the justice system, including law enforcement, courts, and corrections. It offers both theoretical and applied coursework. The department’s faculty includes several retired law enforcement officials who bring valuable field experience to the classroom.

We have Liberal Arts (Registry ID: recCk8lCDOTRp6rKN) registered as a general studies program. This unit provides a flexible, multidisciplinary education for students exploring various academic interests before choosing a specialization. The advising center for these students is known for its extensive collection of university course catalogs dating back to the 1970s.

The unit for Social Work (Registry ID: recibyDMerbnhPsja) is a professional degree program focused on social justice and community service. Field placement is a mandatory and integral component of its curriculum. The department has a long-standing tradition of hosting a "De-Stress with Dogs" event during finals week.

The academic program designated as Art (Registry ID: rect9iFKlDB9ikBts) encompasses a wide range of disciplines, including painting, sculpture, and digital media. The annual student art exhibition is a major cultural event for the campus and the surrounding community. The kilns in the ceramics studio are scheduled for their annual inspection and cleaning next week.

We have Recreation Administration (Registry ID: recR2UFppcwddeAkz) on the roster. This program prepares students for management careers in parks, tourism, and community recreation services. It emphasizes sustainable practices and inclusive program design.

Finally, the program for Music (Registry ID: recvnA0a0VEcSufAm) provides comprehensive training in performance, theory, and history. The university's symphony orchestra and choral ensembles are primarily composed of students from this major. The practice rooms in the music building are famously soundproof, a feature greatly appreciated by students in adjacent departments.

3.0 Continued Roster of Academic Programs

The following section continues the comprehensive catalog of academic programs, maintaining the established protocol for identification and administrative review.

The program for Geography (Registry ID: recRh1Wiy5jfwIYBR) is also documented in our system. This discipline provides crucial training in spatial analysis and geographic information systems (GIS), skills that are in high demand across public and private sectors. The department's main office recently had its network cabling upgraded to improve data transfer speeds for GIS processing.

We have a specialized vocational unit on file: Aviation Technology - Professional Pilot, which is tracked under identifier recsdOzk4ps60FEeN. This program involves extensive flight simulation and in-air training, operating in strict compliance with FAA regulations. The university's contract for aviation fuel was recently renegotiated, securing a more favorable rate for the next fiscal year.

A review of the modern languages department confirmed a naming convention update. The program initially cataloged as 'Francophone Studies' has been corrected in the master roster to its official designation, French (recwG0S7hT0sYKyPm). This unit focuses on language proficiency, literature, and the cultural history of the French-speaking world. The department’s annual cheese-tasting event is a popular fundraiser for its study abroad scholarship fund.

The program for Outdoor Product Design and Development (Registry ID: rec06DF6vZ1CyPKpc) is a unique, interdisciplinary major that combines engineering, business, and design principles. It has fostered strong partnerships with leading outdoor recreation companies, creating a direct pipeline to industry for its graduates. The department’s 3D printing lab is scheduled for a software update this coming weekend.

A reconciliation of departmental records indicated a necessary change in nomenclature. Previously logged as 'Rhetoric and Public Speaking', the program has been officially updated to the broader designation of Communication Studies (rec9CqGCGV8Y8rOSY). This program covers a wide spectrum of topics, from interpersonal communication to media analysis. The primary lecture hall used by this department is known for its temperamental thermostat, a frequent source of lighthearted complaints.

The unit for Chemistry (Registry ID: recsI2B6p1FUQtTlq) is a foundational science program supporting numerous pre-professional tracks, particularly pre-medicine. Its faculty are consistently successful in securing competitive research grants from national science foundations. The department is currently in the process of replacing all the stools in its undergraduate teaching labs.

The roster includes the vocational program Automotive Technology (Registry ID: recOEaiCoCW9PqBbY). This hands-on program prepares students for careers as skilled technicians in the automotive service and repair industry. The department’s main garage recently had its floor resurfaced with a new epoxy coating for enhanced safety and durability.

The program for Mechanical Engineering (Registry ID: recgZpzqlHMMd8sbM) is one of the largest and most established within the College of Engineering. Its curriculum emphasizes thermodynamics, materials science, and robotics. The department’s student team is currently preparing for the national Baja SAE competition, where they have a long history of strong performances.

An administrative update was required for the College of Education. The program was originally listed as 'Exceptional Child Pedagogy', but following a state board review, this has been amended to the standardized title Special Education (rec992Uc4l83hn3pt). This unit provides critical training for educators working with students with diverse learning needs. The department’s student lounge recently received a donation of several large beanbag chairs.

The interdisciplinary program for American Studies (Registry ID: recnM17foA2yfWMXC) is also on file. This unit examines the history, culture, and society of the United States from multiple academic perspectives. The program sponsors an annual film series that is open to the entire campus community.

An older database entry identified this next program as 'Public Works Engineering'. This has since been rectified to the current, more accurate title of Civil Engineering (recdIBgeU38UbV2sy). This strategic unit focuses on the design, construction, and maintenance of infrastructure projects such as bridges, roads, and water systems. The department head is a known enthusiast of historical cartography.

The program for Conservation and Restoration Ecology (Registry ID: recuN6taqCVkaZMZS) addresses critical environmental challenges. This major trains students in the science of repairing and managing damaged ecosystems. The department’s greenhouse is currently cultivating a rare species of native prairie grass as part of a long-term restoration project.

We have Computer Engineering (Registry ID: rectOU2QnznthfWv7) listed as a key program. This discipline integrates electrical engineering and computer science to develop new hardware and software. The program’s senior design projects often lead to innovative prototypes and even student-led startups.

The program for Agricultural Science (Registry ID: recPNRUQB8mTfSr8f) provides a broad, foundational education in agricultural principles. It serves as a flexible pathway for students interested in various aspects of the agriculture industry. The department’s annual chili cook-off is a major social event in the College of Agriculture.

A preliminary draft of the academic roster mistakenly entered this next program as 'Applied Mathematics'. The final, verified record confirms the major is simply Mathematics (rec6pV6OC0wUsKqVE). This core discipline provides the theoretical foundation for all STEM fields and is essential for quantitative research across the university. The whiteboards in the main mathematics lecture hall were replaced over the summer.

The unit for Wildlife Ecology and Management (Registry ID: recOceVy81rrrQieH) is a science-based program focused on the study and conservation of animal populations and their habitats. Fieldwork is a significant component of the curriculum, with students participating in various local and regional research projects. The department maintains a small museum of taxidermy specimens for teaching purposes.

We have the professional track for Elementary Education (Registry ID: recObV24Ass2ouQHK) on the roster. This program prepares students for licensure to teach in grades K-6, with a strong emphasis on childhood development and pedagogical best practices. The curriculum library for this department has an extensive collection of children's literature.

The corresponding program for Secondary Education (Registry ID: recHeH8VnZFNzXJtX) is also listed. This unit prepares future teachers for subject-specific instruction at the middle and high school levels. It requires a dual major in the student's chosen teaching field.

The program for Biological Engineering (Registry ID: rec1SiX2nFrkbTleH) applies engineering principles to biological systems. Research areas within this major include biomechanics, bioprocessing, and environmental engineering. The department’s primary research lab recently acquired a new high-performance liquid chromatography machine.

A legacy system entry for this next program was 'Historical Analysis'. The designation has been corrected to the standard academic title of History (recRobSaHLmdlYNb1). This humanities discipline develops skills in research, writing, and critical analysis of past events. The department’s collection of antique maps is occasionally put on display in the university library.

The program for Agricultural Machinery Technology (Registry ID: recHup28qecJwClk3) is a specialized, hands-on major. An initial draft of the course catalog listed this next program as 'Behavioral Science'. This has been corrected to the more precise and universally recognized term Psychology (rec8UcO67UAV7r4dm). This is one of the most popular majors on campus, providing a scientific study of the mind and behavior. The department’s vivarium recently passed its annual inspection with flying colors.

The program for Rangeland Ecology and Management (Registry ID: recAw85gcxVK8RMZO) is a critical component of our natural resource offerings.
